paragraphs.source_en: Unlike the South African rock art, the interpretation of the Round Head paintings has barely been started. This is mainly due to the scepticism of the scholars studying the Central Saharan rock art, whose general opinion is that the rock art cannot be interpreted without its respective ethnographic record. The only attempt made to interpret it has been using the Lewis-Williams shamanistic theory. This theory, however, does not seem to completely fit the Round Head complex, since there are apparently very few figures or scenes that can be related to people in trance as described for the Southern African rock art. Alternated states of consciousness possibly existing in the Round Head art, probably have other characteristics and forms which still need to be identified.

paragraphs.source_en: A possible interpretation is through the painted sites, in combination with the ethnographic records from various African populations still using rock shelters. Painted sites have been used for specific purposes and supposing that similar functions also occurred during prehistory, we can hypothesize different functions of shelters according to their location, the paintings represented and the archaeological record. In several cases the relationship between paintings and ancient waterfalls is evident and it suggests that the location of the panel was not accidental.

paragraphs.source_en: A special kind of animal was presented, namely an indeterminable quadruped represented always with the head downwards. Very similar indeterminable animals exist in the South African rock art where they are interpreted as animals of the rain, and similar interpretation cannot be excluded for the Round Head quadrupeds. Mouflon and antelope are predominant animals in the Round Head art and their importance is evident also from their association with presumed ritual scenes, their direct association to human figures and their body decoration, which is similar to that of anthropomorphic figures. Lastly, the probable role of body attributes is outlined suggesting different social statuses within the population producing the Round Head art.
